subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trusted lifecycle for generated HTML after outbound media staging?
rationale: The code path is a narrow fix for a real message-loss regression, but it deliberately authorizes a new host-read HTML trust path outside the temp root; automation cannot accept that security boundary on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Accept Provenance Lifecycle
options.body: Merge after a security/area owner confirms that realpath plus sha256/size provenance is the intended trust contract for staged generated HTML.

options.title: Require More Hardening
options.body: Ask the author to add lifecycle constraints such as TTL-based row pruning or chunked prune deletion before merge.

options.title: Reject Boundary Expansion
options.body: Close or replace the PR with a different delivery design that avoids trusting staged HTML paths at all.

recommendation.title: Accept Provenance Lifecycle
recommendation.body: Merge after a security/area owner confirms that realpath plus sha256/size provenance is the intended trust contract for staged generated HTML.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the original trusted generated HTML host-read seam that this PR extends.
